MCD.rationale: McDonald's is a high-quality franchise with best-in-class operating margins (~45-46%), a 95% franchised model generating predictable cash flows, and a strong brand moat. Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +9.4%, EPS +6.9%) and 3.8% global comparable sales growth. However, the stock has declined ~17% from its February highs, and the near-term trajectory is mixed: QoQ metrics show sequential deceleration (revenue -7.9%, EPS -12.6%), the CEO flagged consumer spending 'getting a little bit worse,' and Q2 is expected to see weaker sales due to tough comps. The balance sheet carries negative equity (-$1.29B) reflecting heavy leverage, though this is structural to the franchise/real estate model. Valuation appears reasonable at ~23x P/E (lowest in ~2 years per news), and the stock is near its 52-week low of $271.98, suggesting some of the headwinds may be priced in. The dividend yield of ~2.6% and 50-year streak of increases provide support. However, rising interest rates (10Y at 4.45%), elevated oil prices ($92.65/bbl), and consumer spending headwinds create a challenging macro backdrop. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists to drive a re-rating. The score reflects a solid but mature business at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation, tempered by macro headwinds and lack of a near-term catalyst.
